urgency.label: Pressure
urgency.tip: Real organisations don't need an answer in minutes. Pause, then verify through an official channel.

threat.label: Threat
threat.tip: Don't react to threats. Contact the company using the number on your card, bill or official website, not the one in the message.

prize.label: Prize
prize.tip: You can't win a contest you never entered. Ignore it.

credentials.label: Secret codes
credentials.tip: Never share OTPs, PINs, CVVs or passwords. Banks and delivery firms never ask for them by message or call.

payment.label: Payment
payment.tip: Never pay a 'fee' to receive a prize, parcel, loan or job. Don't send gift cards, crypto or wire transfers to people you haven't met.

impersonation.label: Impersonation
impersonation.tip: Check the claim yourself: open the official app or type the website address manually.

secrecy.label: Secrecy
secrecy.tip: Scammers try to isolate you. Talk to someone you trust before acting.

contact_switch.label: Channel switch
contact_switch.tip: Be careful when a stranger moves the chat to WhatsApp or Telegram.

investment.label: Investment
investment.tip: Guaranteed returns don't exist. Check any firm with your country's financial regulator.

job.label: Job offer
job.tip: Genuine employers don't charge fees or promise big pay for simple tasks.

family.label: Family request
family.tip: Call the person on the number you already have before sending any money.

tech_support.label: Tech support
tech_support.tip: Phones and browsers don't call you or show phone numbers for 'virus' alerts. Close the page.

click.label: Link
click.tip: Don't tap links in unexpected messages. Type the official address yourself.

url.label: Link
url.tip: Don't tap the link. Type the official address yourself.

rules.title: Artificial deadline
rules.explain: Scammers rush you so you don't stop to think.

rules.title: Threat to block or close an account
rules.explain: Fear of losing access is the most common pressure tactic.
examples: Your account will be suspended today

rules.title: Legal or police threat
rules.explain: Genuine authorities don't threaten arrest by text message.
examples: A warrant has been issued for your arrest

rules.title: Unexpected prize or winnings
rules.explain: You can't win a contest you never entered.

rules.title: Asks for secret codes or personal details
rules.explain: Banks, couriers and tax offices never ask for OTPs, PINs or passwords by message.
examples: Please share your OTP to continue
Verify your account to avoid closure

rules.title: Asks for a small fee
rules.explain: Advance fees are how prize, parcel, loan and job scams make money.
examples: A small processing fee is required

rules.title: Unusual payment method
rules.explain: Gift cards, crypto and wire transfers are hard to reverse, so scammers love them.
examples: Buy iTunes gift cards and send me the codes

rules.title: Asks you to send money
rules.explain: A request for quick money from someone claiming to be a friend or relative is a classic scam.
examples: Can you please send me some money today

rules.title: Fake delivery notice
rules.explain: Delivery-fee texts are one of the most common scams worldwide.
patterns: \b(parcel|package|shipment|delivery|order)\b.{0,50}\b(on hold|held|could not be delivered|couldn't be delivered|undelivered|failed|pending|returned|incomplete address|customs)\b
examples: Your parcel is on hold, update your address

rules.title: Generic 'official' wording
rules.explain: Real organisations use your name. Generic greetings and vague 'security team' claims are a warning sign.
examples: Dear customer, our security team noticed suspicious activity

rules.title: 'New number' family message
rules.explain: Scammers pose as a child or parent on a new number and ask for urgent money.
patterns: \bhi\s+(mum|mom|dad|mother|father)\b.{0,80}\b(new number|lost my phone|broke my phone|new phone)\b
examples: Hi mum, this is my new number

rules.title: Asks you to keep it secret
rules.explain: Secrecy stops friends and family from spotting the scam.

rules.title: Pushes you to WhatsApp or Telegram
rules.explain: Moving the chat to a private app helps scammers avoid detection.
examples: Message us on WhatsApp to begin

rules.title: Big pay for easy work
rules.explain: High pay for simple tasks is the hallmark of job scams.

rules.title: Typical job-scam wording
rules.explain: Vague, no-experience offers that find you first are rarely real jobs.

rules.title: Guaranteed investment returns
rules.explain: No legitimate investment can guarantee profit.

rules.title: Fake virus or hacking alert
rules.explain: Scareware tries to get you to call a fake support line or install remote-access software.
examples: Your computer has been infected with a virus

rules.title: Asks you to tap a link
rules.explain: Unexpected links are the main way phishing works.

rules.title: Standard anti-fraud wording
rules.explain: Genuine one-time-code messages usually include a warning like this. It doesn't prove the message is real, but it's a good sign.
examples: Your OTP is 482913. Do not share it with anyone.

rules.title: Plazo artificial
rules.explain: Los estafadores te apuran para que no pienses.

rules.title: Amenaza de bloqueo
rules.explain: El miedo a perder el acceso es la presión más común.

rules.title: Premio inesperado
rules.explain: No puedes ganar un sorteo en el que no participaste.

rules.title: Pide claves o datos personales
rules.explain: Ningún banco pide códigos o contraseñas por mensaje.

rules.title: Pago inusual o tarifa
rules.explain: Las tarjetas de regalo y las criptomonedas son difíciles de recuperar.
